preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= n for x in stdin.split() if x.isdigit())
preconditions.description: Every integer in the input is between 1 and n (inclusive), where n is the first integer in the test case.

preconditions.expression: all(q[i] >= q[i-1] for i in range(1, len(q))) if len(q) > 1 else True
preconditions.description: The array q is non-decreasing, as it is derived from a permutation's prefix maxima.
The length of q matches the given n for each test case.
The first element of q is at least 1 and at most n.

preconditions.expression: all(q[i] <= n for i in range(len(q)))
preconditions.description: Every element in q is at most n.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= n for x in min_perm.split()) and all(1 <= int(x) <= n for x in max_perm.split())
postconditions.description: Both the lexicographically minimal and maximal permutations contain integers between 1 and n (inclusive).
Both permutations have length exactly n.

postconditions.expression: all(int(min_perm.split()[i]) <= q[i] for i in range(n)) and all(int(max_perm.split()[i]) <= q[i] for i in range(n))
postconditions.description: For each index i, the i-th element of both permutations is less than or equal to q[i], as q[i] is the max of the first i elements of the permutation.

postconditions.expression: all(int(min_perm.split()[i]) == q[i] or any(int(min_perm.split()[j]) == q[i] for j in range(i)) for i in range(n))
postconditions.description: For each index i in the minimal permutation, the i-th element is either equal to q[i] or there exists a previous element equal to q[i], ensuring q[i] is the max of the first i elements.

postconditions.expression: all(int(max_perm.split()[i]) == q[i] or any(int(max_perm.split()[j]) == q[i] for j in range(i)) for i in range(n))
postconditions.description: For each index i in the maximal permutation, the i-th element is either equal to q[i] or there exists a previous element equal to q[i], ensuring q[i] is the max of the first i elements.

postconditions.expression: all(int(min_perm.split()[i]) != int(min_perm.split()[j]) for i in range(n) for j in range(i))
postconditions.description: The minimal permutation contains all integers from 1 to n exactly once.

postconditions.expression: all(int(max_perm.split()[i]) != int(max_perm.split()[j]) for i in range(n) for j in range(i))
postconditions.description: The maximal permutation contains all integers from 1 to n exactly once.
The minimal permutation is lexicographically less than or equal to the maximal permutation.

postconditions.expression: all(int(min_perm.split()[i]) <= int(max_perm.split()[i]) for i in range(n))
postconditions.description: For each index i, the i-th element of the minimal permutation is less than or equal to the i-th element of the maximal permutation.

postconditions.expression: all(int(min_perm.split()[i]) == q[i] == int(max_perm.split()[i]) or (int(min_perm.split()[i]) != q[i] and int(max_perm.split()[i]) != q[i]) for i in range(n))
postconditions.description: For each index i, if q[i] is not the first occurrence of its value in the permutation, then both minimal and maximal permutations have the same value at i (the smallest or largest available number not yet used).
